subject: Assistance Needed with PCA at Different Temperatures in AMBER

messages.author: ABDELATIF MESSAOUDI
messages.body:
Dear AMBER Users,
To address a question from a reviewer regarding Principal Component
Analysis (PCA) at different temperatures, I followed the tutorial available
at the following link:
https://ambermd.org/tutorials/advanced/tutorial41/
I have attached my input file, Python script, and the resulting image for
your reference.
Could you please advise if this approach is correct, or if there is
anything else I should consider?
Thank you for your assistance.
Best regards,
Abdelatif Messaoudi
University of Batna 1,Algeria

messages.author: Carlos Simmerling
messages.body:
It will help if you can share what information you want to learn, otherwise
we can only direct you to the manual and tutorials. What is it about your
data that you want to understand using PCA at different temperatures?

messages.author: Carlos Simmerling
messages.body:
I think PCA could be helpful depending on the motions in your system. I
would suggest that you carry out a single PCA analysis on the full
trajectory data including all temperatures though. If you do pca separately
it is difficult to compare them. Then you can project each temperature
separately, using the same vectors.
See this tutorial:
https://amberhub.chpc.utah.edu/introduction-to-principal-component-analysis/
